title: finding(data-objectstack): the README's "Concurrent Access" bullet states the opposite of what MetadataCache does, and a test pins the opposite
body:
`packages/data-objectstack/README.md`, under **Cache Configuration**, tells a reader:

> **Concurrent Access**: Handles async operations safely. Note that concurrent requests for the same uncached key may result in multiple fetcher calls.

That is the opposite of what the cache does. `MetadataCache.get` keeps an in-flight
`Promise` map: the first caller for an uncached key invokes the fetcher, every
concurrent caller for the same key is handed the SAME promise and increments a
`coalesced` counter, and the slot is cleared in a `finally` so a rejection does not
poison retries. `MetadataCacheStats` publishes `coalesced` for exactly this reason,
and the class docblock says so in as many words.

## The named probe

Not inferred from reading the code — the repository already pins the opposite of the
sentence:

- `packages/data-objectstack/src/cache/MetadataCache.test.ts` — `should coalesce
  concurrent fetches for the same key`: three concurrent `get` calls for one uncached
  key, asserting the fetcher ran **once** and `stats.coalesced === 2`.
- `packages/data-objectstack/src/cache/MetadataCache.test.ts` — `should clear inflight
  slot after fetch rejection so retries are possible`.

Run: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/data-objectstack/src/cache/MetadataCache.test.ts`
(green on `main` at 93127bd6f).

## How it got stale

The bullet landed in `e59c76e08` (2026-01-30). Coalescing landed three months later in
`03bdcc03b` (2026-05-01, `this.inflight`) and the README sentence was never revisited.
So this is an ERROR rather than an omission: the sentence was true when written and is
false now, and a reader budgeting for duplicate fetches (or writing a fetcher defensively
idempotent because the README told them to) is designing against behaviour the package
no longer has.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed in passing

Found while implementing objectui#8320, whose file surface is `MetadataCache`'s class
docblock, one stale ledger row and a changeset. This is a different file, a different
defect and a prose rewrite rather than a mechanical edit, so it is not a bounded
in-place fix. It is also **not** covered by the objectui#8258 example gate or by
`check-doc-snippet-types`: both judge fenced CODE, and this is a bullet.

## Severity

Low, and documentation-truth rather than runtime — nothing breaks. Note the difference
from objectui#8320 though: that block lived in a docblock that never reaches
`dist/*.d.ts`, whereas `README.md` IS in the package's published `files[]`, so this
sentence ships to npm.

Filed unassigned and unlabelled beyond `finding`; triage owns the priority. Written by
an agent seat while implementing objectui#8320.
